# usage: watch.py target seconds [interval] -- prints time since start whenever first line of pane changes
import subprocess, sys, time

start = time.time(); last = None
while time.time() - start < dur:
    out = subprocess.run(['tmux','capture-pane','-t',target,'-p'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout

        print("%.2f %r" % (time.time()-start, first)); last = first
    time.sleep(iv)
EOF

#!/bin/sh
# Build the tty-clock reimplementation into ./executable
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

have_cc=0
command -v cc >/dev/null 2>&1 && have_cc=1
have_hdr=0
for h in /usr/include/ncurses.h /usr/include/ncurses/ncurses.h /usr/include/curses.h /usr/local/include/ncurses.h; do
    [ -f "$h" ] && have_hdr=1
done

# Best effort: install a C compiler and the ncurses development files if missing.
if [ "$have_cc" = 0 ] || [ "$have_hdr" = 0 ]; then
    SUDO=""
    [ "$(id -u)" != 0 ] && command -v sudo >/dev/null 2>&1 && SUDO="sudo"
    if command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        $SUDO apt-get update -qq || true
        $SUDO apt-get install -y -qq gcc libc6-dev libncurses-dev || \
        $SUDO apt-get install -y -qq gcc libc6-dev libncurses5-dev || true
    elif command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        $SUDO dnf install -y gcc ncurses-devel || true
    elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        $SUDO yum install -y gcc ncurses-devel || true
    elif command -v apk >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        $SUDO apk add gcc musl-dev ncurses-dev || true
    elif command -v pacman >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        $SUDO pacman -Sy --noconfirm gcc ncurses || true
    fi
fi

CC=${CC:-cc}
CFLAGS="-O2 -Wall"

# Compile from inside src/ so that __FILE__ is the bare file name.
cd src
if ! $CC $CFLAGS -o ../executable ttyclock.c -lncurses 2>/dev/null; then
    if ! $CC $CFLAGS -o ../executable ttyclock.c -lncurses -ltinfo 2>/dev/null; then
        $CC $CFLAGS -o ../executable ttyclock.c -lncursesw
    fi
fi
cd ..
chmod +x executable
EOF
chmod +x compile.sh; rm -f executable; ./compile.sh && ls -la executable && ./executable -v
